name: Devpost

sources.title: Devpost Projects gallery — 'Add your project' button links to /software/new?flow[name]=add_software
Add-software flow — redirects to login; OAuth via GitHub/Facebook/Google/LinkedIn or email

conditions: Free to add a project, but requires a Devpost account — /software/new redirects to the login/register page
requirements: Publish a real software project — the Projects gallery is for things you built (hackathon entries and portfolio projects)
Account creation via GitHub, Facebook, Google, LinkedIn OAuth, or email at secure.devpost.com/users/register
Hackathon submissions are a separate flow governed by each hackathon's rules and deadlines
preparation: Links: repo URL, live/demo URL, video demo
Built-with tags (the gallery is browsable by tech like python, react, flutter, gemini)
workflow: Sign up or log in (OAuth or email)
From devpost.com/software click 'Add your project' (goes to /software/new?flow[name]=add_software)
Fill project name, description/story, built-with tags, repo and demo links, images/video
Publish — the project appears in the Projects gallery and on your portfolio
Optionally attach it to a hackathon submission via that hackathon's own flow
watchFor: The software gallery skews to hackathon projects — a polished commercial SaaS can look out of place; frame it as a project
Outbound links are nofollow per prior source data — value is developer-community exposure, not link equity
Project pages rank via Devpost's own featured/tags system; weak built-with tags bury the entry
countsAsLive: A public project page exists at devpost.com/software/<slug> and appears in the Projects gallery/profile
unknowns: Exact form fields inside the logged-in add-software flow
Whether moderation removes non-hackathon commercial products
